args.command:
cat > /tmp/t/fmt/NOTES.md <<'NOTES_EOF'
# lnav v0.14.0 — Log Format Detection & Parsing Findings

Binary: `/workspace/executable`. All tests run headless: `-n -N [files] [-c ';SQL']`.
Machine clock during tests: 2026-08-08 (UTC timezone). Working dir `/tmp/t/fmt`, samples in `samples/`.

## 1. Format discovery

- No `lnav_log_formats` / `lnav_formats` / `formats` SQL table exists. `sqlite_master` queries return
  **empty output** (lnav appears to block/hide it; `EXIT=0`, no error).
- SQL errors print to stdout like:
  ```
    error: failed to compile SQL statement
   reason: no such table: lnav_log_formats
   --> command-option:1
   | SELECT * FROM lnav_log_formats
  ```
  and still exit 0.
- Management mode (`-m`) usage:
  - `-m` alone → `error: expecting an operation to perform` + list of operations:
    `apps`, `config`, `format`, `piper`, `regex101`, `crash` (exit 0).
  - `-m format` (no name) → prints full built-in format list (79 formats):
    access_log, alb_log, block_log, bro, bunyan_log, caddy_log, candlepin_log,
    choose_repo_log, cloudflare_json_log, cloudvm_ram_log, cups_log, dpkg_log,
    ecs_log, elb_log, engine_log, env_logger_log, error_log, esx_syslog_log,
    fsck_hfs_log, generic_log, github_events_log, glog_log, haproxy_log, idea_log,
    java_log, journald_json_log, katello_log, laravel_log, lnav_debug_log,
    lnav_piper_log, logcat_log, logfmt_log, macosuni_log, mongodb_json_log,
    mysql_error_log, mysql_gen_log, mysql_slow_log, nextcloud, nextflow_log,
    openamdb_log, openam_log, openstack_log, otel_collector_log, otlp_python_log,
    page_log, pcap_log, pino_log, postgres_log, procstate_log, proxifier_log,
    rails_log, redis_log, robot_fwk_log, rust_tracing_log, s3_log, simple_rs_log,
    snaplogic_log, spdlog_log, sssd_log, strace_log, syslog_log, tcf_log,
    tcsh_history, unifi_log, uwsgi_log, vdsm_log, vmk_log, vmw_log, vmw_py_log,
    vmw_vc_svc_log, vpostgres_log, w3c_log, web_robot_log, xmlrpc_log,
    zap_console_log, zellijFmt, zookeeper_log
  - `-m format <name>` (no op) → error + description + regex names, e.g.
    `syslog_log: The system logger format found on most posix systems. Regexes: rfc5424, std`.
    Operations: `get`, `test`, `source`, `sources`, `regex`.
  - `-m format generic_log get` → `generic_log: <no description>`;
    `regex`/`source` → `error: "generic_log" is an internal format that is not defined in a configuration file`.
  - `-m format syslog_log test samples/syslog_std.log` →
    `test file matched format pattern std` + echoed first matching line with file:line ref.
  - `-m format <name> regex` lists regex names; the only sub-op is `regex101` (needs network; not used).
  - `-m apps` → only op `create`. `-m config` → `get`, `blame`, `file-options`.
    `-m piper` → `list`, `clean`. `-m crash` → `upload`.

## 2. Detection results (via `;SELECT filepath, mimetype, format, lines FROM lnav_file`)

`lnav_file` columns: `device, inode, filepath, mimetype, content_id, format, lines, time_offset, options_path, options`.
Recognized logs get `mimetype=text/log`; plain text `text/plain` with `format=<NULL>`.

| Sample | Detected format |
|---|---|
| `Jul  5 10:23:01 host proc[123]: msg` | `syslog_log` |
| `<13>1 2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z host app pid msgid - msg` (RFC5424) | `syslog_log` |
| apache combined / common / vhost (`vhost:port ` prefix) | `access_log` (all three) |
| `2024-01-02 03:04:05,123 INFO msg` | `generic_log` |
| `2024-01-02T03:04:05.123456+00:00 msg`, `[2024-01-02 03:04:05] msg`, `...T...Z msg` | `generic_log` |
| log4j-style `2024-01-02 03:04:05,123 INFO  [main] c.e.App - msg` | `generic_log` (NOT java_log) |
| python `2024-01-01 00:00:00,000 - name - INFO - msg` | `generic_log` (see quirks) |
| `{"timestamp":..,"level":..,"message":..}` | `rust_tracing_log` (!) |
| `{"ts":..,"level":..,"msg":..}` | `caddy_log` (!) |
| `{"time":"2024-01-02 03:04:05.123","level":..,"message":..}` | `nextcloud` (!) |
| `time=... level=info msg=...` | `logfmt_log` |
| `10:23:01.123456 open(...) = 3` | `strace_log` |
| `#+<epoch>` + command lines | `tcsh_history` |
| `I0102 03:04:05.123456 12345 file.cc:100] msg` | `glog_log` |

JSON-lines: whichever JSON format's regex matches first wins; there is no dedicated "generic JSON log"
format — generic `{"timestamp","level","message"}` lines are claimed by `rust_tracing_log`.

### Parsed columns observed

- `syslog_log` (std): `log_line, log_time, log_level, log_hostname, log_msgid, log_pid, log_pri,
  log_procname, log_struct, log_syslog_tag, syslog_version` + common cols
  (`log_part, log_idle_msecs, log_mark, log_comment, log_tags, log_annotations, log_filters`).
  - std regex fills `log_hostname, log_procname, log_pid, log_syslog_tag` (`proc[pid]`), `log_pri/msgid/struct/version` NULL.
  - rfc5424 fills `log_pri` (13), `log_msgid` (ID47), `syslog_version` (1), `log_struct` (`-` or the SD block verbatim).
- `access_log`: `c_ip, cs_method, cs_referer, cs_uri_query, cs_uri_stem, cs_user_agent, cs_username,
  cs_version, sc_bytes, sc_status, cs_host`. `-` fields → NULL. vhost line fills `cs_host`
  (port stripped: `example.com:80` → `example.com`). `log_level`: 2xx→info, 404→error.
- `generic_log`: `log_line, log_time, log_level, log_body` (+ common cols). Body = line minus matched
  timestamp/level prefix.
- `logfmt_log`: `fields` column = JSON object of extra kv pairs (`{"user":"bob"}`); `time/level/msg`
  consumed into standard columns.
- `strace_log`: `pid, duration, errno, rc, rc_extra, syscall, siginfo, signame`. Time-only stamps
  (`10:23:01.123456`) get today's date.
- `tcsh_history`: only `#+<epoch>` lines produce rows (`log_line` = file line of the `#+` line,
  e.g. 0 and 2); the command line is the body.
- `glog_log`: `level` (letter I/E), `src_file, src_line, thread`; year inferred (current year).
- `rust_tracing_log` (claimed our JSON): `level, target, message, threadName, threadId`. NOTE: each
  input line produced log_line steps of 2 (0, 2) and `lnav_file.lines=4` for a 2-line file — the
  format renders messages as 2 physical lines (log_text contains embedded newlines `␊`).
- `caddy_log`: many caddy-specific columns (`logger, request/client_ip, ...`); our `ts/msg` values landed
  in `msg`, level string preserved verbatim (`warning` stayed `warning`).
- `nextcloud`: `exception, app, reqId, ...` all NULL for our input; level from `level` key.

## 3. log_level detection

### syslog_log
- PRI/severity is **ignored** for level: `<11>1` (sev 3 = error) with plain body → `info`.
- Level comes from keyword scan of the message body: word `error` anywhere (case-insensitive,
  word-boundary: "terror" does NOT trigger, "word error word" DOES) → `error`;
  `warning`/`warn` → `warning`; **everything else → `info`** (debug/trace/fatal/critical/notice/err/crit
  all stay `info` in syslog bodies). Body is never modified.

### generic_log
- Observed level vocabulary: `trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical, fatal, notice, stats,
  unknown` (also `warn` appears in the canned `lnav_example_log` demo table).
- **Pattern lock-in per file**: generic_log has several internal patterns; whichever pattern matches
  the FIRST line is used for the whole file. Lines that don't match the locked pattern (even if they
  have timestamps) are **appended to the previous message** as continuation lines.
- Pattern families observed:

  (`an error occurred mid-sentence` merged/unknown in generic).

- **Continuation lines**: any line not matching the file's locked pattern is appended to the previous
  message's `log_body`/`log_text` joined by newline (`␊` in output). Works for syslog (indented stack
  traces AND non-indented lines) and generic_log. `log_line` = file line number of the message START
  (so it jumps: 0, 3, 5). `lnav_file.lines` counts physical lines.
- **Leading non-timestamped lines**: a file starting with non-matching lines gets a row with
  `log_body=NULL, log_level=unknown` and `log_time` = the time of the first following message.
- **Syslog year inference**: always the CURRENT year — no "future dates roll back a year" logic.
  `Dec 25` in August 2026 → `2026-12-25` (future kept as-is). Same for Aug 9 (1 day future).
- **Monotonic clamping**: within a file, if a parsed timestamp is earlier than the previous message,
  `log_time` is clamped forward to the previous message's time. `log_actual_time` keeps the true parsed
  value. Verified with apache lines (e.g. `+0530` line parsed 06:30 after a 19:00 line →
  log_time=19:00:00.000000, log_actual_time=06:30).
- **YEAR-2000 BUG**: dates in year 2000 on/after Mar 1 are shifted +1 day (10/Oct/2000 → 2000-10-11;
  15/Jun/2000 → 2000-06-16; 31/Dec/2000 → 2001-01-01; Jan/Feb 2000 incl. Feb 29 are correct). Other
  years incl. other leap years (1996, 2024, 2100) are fine. Quirk of the normal parse path;
  out-of-order (clamped) lines showed the correct 2000-10-10 in `log_actual_time`.
- `log_time` display format: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff` (µs). `log_time_msecs` = epoch milliseconds
  (e.g. 1783246981000). `log_idle_msecs` = ms since previous message (0 for first; continuations
  don't reset it — measured between message start times).
- tz offsets honored: `13:55:36 -0700` → 20:55:36 UTC; output is in machine-local (UTC here).

  print all their lines), ordered by `(log_time, log_line)`. Verified: two files, same timestamp →

## Summary of key findings

**1. Format discovery** — No `lnav_log_formats`/`lnav_formats` table; `sqlite_master` queries return empty (blocked). Use `-m format` (no name) which lists all **79 built-in formats** (access_log, syslog_log, generic_log, logfmt_log, strace_log, tcsh_history, glog_log, java_log, caddy_log, rust_tracing_log, nextcloud, …). `-m format <name>` gives description + regex names; ops are `get/test/source/sources/regex`. `generic_log` is internal (no dumpable config). SQL errors print a formatted `error:/reason:` block but exit 0.

**2. Detection** — Verified via `lnav_file` (columns: device, inode, filepath, mimetype, content_id, format, lines, time_offset, options_path, options): BSD + RFC5424 syslog → `syslog_log`; apache combined/common/vhost all → `access_log`; all plain timestamp variants → `generic_log` (log4j- and python-logging-style included); logfmt → `logfmt_log`; strace/tcsh/glog detected. Surprise: generic JSON-lines are claimed by specific formats — `{timestamp,level,message}` → `rust_tracing_log`, `{ts,level,msg}` → `caddy_log`, `{time,level,message}` → `nextcloud`. Parsed columns per format recorded in NOTES.md (syslog fills hostname/procname/pid/tag; access_log fills c_ip, cs_*, sc_*; logfmt stashes extra kv into a `fields` JSON column).

**3. Levels** — syslog: PRI ignored; body scanned for word `error`→error, `warn/warning`→warning, everything else→info. generic_log: **locks onto one of several internal patterns based on the file's first line** (full-ts+level, `[LEVEL]`, `LEVEL:`, date-only); non-matching lines become continuations of the previous message. Full-ts pattern levels {error,err,warning,warn,info,debug,trace} (consumed from body); date-only pattern also recognizes fatal, critical, notice, stats(1/2/5), verbose→trace (kept in body); `crit`→unknown. Vocabulary observed: trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical, fatal, notice, stats, unknown.

**4. Timestamps** — Continuation lines merge into previous message (`log_line` = start line, jumps 0,3,5). Leading un-timestamped lines get a NULL-body row stamped with the first message's time. **Syslog year = always current year, no future-rollover** (Dec 25 in August → same-year future). **Out-of-order timestamps are clamped forward** (`log_time` monotonic; `log_actual_time` keeps truth). **Year-2000 bug: dates ≥ Mar 1 2000 shift +1 day** (only year 2000; other leap years fine). `log_time_msecs` = epoch ms; `log_idle_msecs` = gap to previous message.

**5. Default headless output** — Raw lines of the log view, ordered by `(log_time, log_line)` (equal timestamps interleave files round-robin by line number, independent of arg order). If any log file exists, only the log view prints (text args suppressed); text-only → only the LAST text file prints. Binary → hexdump view. Empty → nothing, exit 0. No-trailing-newline and CRLF handled (`\r` stripped). `.gz`/`.bz2`/`.zip` transparently decompressed (zip member path `archive/inner`). Directory arg loads top-level files; `-r` recurses.

**6. Errors** — Nonexistent file: `error: unable to open file: <path>` / `reason: No such file or directory`, exit 1, and no output even if other files are valid. Unreadable file untestable (session runs as root).

**7/8. Schema** — `all_logs` has hidden columns (log_path, log_text, log_body, log_actual_time, log_time_msecs) absent from `SELECT *`, plus message-clustering columns `log_msg_format`/`log_msg_values` (variables→`#`, values→JSON). Plain text has no table (format NULL). Views: log, text, help, histogram, db, schema, pretty, spectro, timeline; `lnav_views` and `lnav_top_view` are queryable.

Open items noted in NOTES.md: exact generic_log pattern set/priority (internal, not dumpable), root cause of the year-2000 quirk, and possible additional level names.
